THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  69

was one of the incorporators of the Plainsman Literary Society of Savoy College in 1884. For the next year, 1885-1886, the commercial department was in charge of Mr. W. P. Macy, who also taught French and Applied Mathematics. Mr. Lewis J. Reynolds, a Senior student in the B.S. course, was one of the faculty 1886-1887 as Professor of Business Penmanship.

The first music teacher listed in College advertising of 1884-1885 were Miss Maggie Toms, who was listed for 1885. Next was Miss Kate Hendershot, who was listed for the school year 1885-1886 in the advertising from Savoy, the College's own training, came to the faculty as Professor of English and Literature. As a student in the College Miss Fannie Jackson taught in a College studio. It is recalled that she was a music teacher. Miss Fannie Chenoweth taught during the year 1880-1890, and Mrs. H. H. Halbell taught for the year of that year. Mrs. Chenoweth (now Mrs. S. P. Smith) and Mrs. Pritchett (now Mrs. Thomas E. Murphy) are good musicians in the studios near the campus, were Mrs. Jed Williams, from the earliest days of the early nineties and Miss Lottie Daniels, in 1888-1890, and Miss Lottie Daniels, about four or five. First teachers in the primary department later were Misses from Bonham, who were Miss Jennie Lacy, of Bonham, who taught the last year of the school's existence.

FINANCIAL ADMINISTRATION.—A study of the financial management of the Savoy College reveals two contrasting phases of President Halbell's management: one the courage and persistence of a man who was deeply devoted to the institution, entirely without endowment and dependent on the income from tuition for its support; the other the one seen in Mr. Halbell a courageous and sagacious financial manager; he began to show in the writing the extent that the magnanimous and philanthropic activities shown in the welfare of the College.
